# test_reverse_words.py
# Replace `your_module` with the module where reverse_words is defined.
import pytest

from your_module import reverse_words


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("input_s", "expected"),
    [
        ("hello world", "world hello"),
        ("the quick brown fox", "fox brown quick the"),
        ("hello", "hello"),
        ("hello, world!", "world! hello,"),
        ("café naïve", "naïve café"),
    ],
)
def test_reverse_words_happy_path(input_s, expected):
    assert reverse_words(input_s) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("input_s", "expected"),
    [
        ("", ""),
        ("   ", ""),
        ("\t\n\r", ""),
        ("  hello  ", "hello"),
        ("  hello   world  ", "world hello"),
        ("hello\tworld\npython", "python world hello"),
        ("a  b    c", "c b a"),
    ],
)
def test_reverse_words_edge_cases(input_s, expected):
    assert reverse_words(input_s) == expected


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "bad_input",
    [
        None,
        123,
        ["hello", "world"],
        {"text": "hello world"},
    ],
)
def test_reverse_words_non_string_without_split_raises_attribute_error(bad_input):
    with pytest.raises(AttributeError):
        reverse_words(bad_input)


def test_reverse_words_bytes_raise_type_error():
    # bytes has .split(), but returns bytes elements, which str.join cannot join.
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        reverse_words(b"hello world")
